reason: Schedule and feasibility lens. The idea can be built and the calendar has room, but a scored probe by 29 Sep 10:00 UTC is far below 70% as written. CHECKED: (a) tracksdata 0.1.0rc9 (the version our notes record as Kaggle site-packages) has ILPSolver(node_weight=..., timeout=...) (_ilp_solver.py l.134-159; overlap constraints l.330/403), so node_weight=NodeAttr('hyp_cost') is valid. (b) Our ILP call has no node weight (tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py l.562-567). (c) +1% nodes = -0.0009 is right (0.1 x 1% x ~0.91). (d) Low peaks are max-pool local maxima of the same logits, so free peaks are separated from standard peaks by the pool window (predict script l.256-296). (e) A toy ILP benchmark in this container (tracksdata + ilpy + SCIP, 1 thread) went from 12.1 s to 19.2 s when +31% hypothesis nodes were added (+63% edges). It scales smoothly; no blow-up. BLOCKERS: (1) Sequential gating. The idea runs only if H1 step 0 passes AND H1's lab shows that geometry cannot place the pool nodes. H1's lab ends 26 Sep ~04:00 at the earliest (agent push) and ~10:00-12:00 more realistically (user push, sibling verdict v_literature_byte-lowscore-extension_schedule.json). H2 then needs its own GPU pass on train, because hypotheses change the edge transformer's input and so every edge_prob. After that come its own lab gate (the idea's own P(>= +0.002) = 0.15) and a probe. Estimates (all guesses): P(x138 base) 0.85 x P(H1 route opens) ~0.3 x P(build + runtime OK) 0.75 x P(lab gate) 0.2-0.3 x P(calendar) 0.9 = ~0.03-0.05. Dropping every gate and submitting it anyway still gives only 0.85 x 0.75 x 0.9 = ~0.57. (2) The insertion point is fragile. Edges are made inside predict_video, so hypotheses must enter at the `arr = _detect_cells_pooled(...)` line. That line is also the anchor for readmit's lowdet dump patch AND the V1284 head patch, and the x138 notebook records an earlier anchor collision that silently disabled the dump (exp56 cell 4, notebook l.1610-1616). The ILP change must re-anchor on x138's already-patched solver block (the timeout patch, same cell), and build_graph must carry a new node attribute. --base x138 in tools/build_probe_kernel.py accepts only divinsert/leafprune (CONTEXT l.1509). Realistic effort: 5-6 agent-h for the patch and tests, plus 3-4 agent-h for an x138-on-train lab harness, which does not exist (sibling verdicts). (3) Runtime risk is mis-stated. The ILP timeout is not a catastrophic fallback: SCIP returns its incumbent (experiments/ext_x138/DIFF.md l.88). The real catastrophic channels are REPAIR_DEADLINE_S = 27000 s, which switches off relink, readmit, gapfill, safe divisions and linefit for every later video, and the 12 h hard limit. Scaling the toy result to x138 graphs (~30k raw nodes per video; 121,777 on 4 dummy clips, CONTEXT l.1515) adds a guessed +25-40 s of ILP per video plus more edge-transformer work. Over ~100-130 hidden videos on 2 shards that is +0.5-1 h wall time, against a scoring run we observe at ~7.5 h, right at the 7.5 h guard. The hidden x138 runtime is unknown until #34 finishes. (4) GPU contention. vitalii has 0 GPU-h until 26 Sep 00:00 and 30 per week after that. Friend A has been silent since 24 Sep. The x138 lab lines already requested (H1 6-7 h, divins-retune 13-16 h, dense-proposal 3.5-4 h) oversubscribe the week before this second inference pass (4-7 GPU-h) is counted. (5) The expected gain (+0.000..+0.003, a guess) is at or below the LB noise of 0.003, so even a scored probe would barely inform the finals.
fix_if_any: Make it a decoupled, runtime-safe rider that is gated once. (i) Drop the sequential dependency on H1's lab result. Put the hypothesis arm in the SAME x138-on-train lab kernel as H1 from the start: control = x138 verbatim (shared with H1); hyp arm = a second predict pass per video with the free 0.5-0.965 peaks appended at the arr line BEFORE the V1284 refine, so they also get refined. Dump the candidate graph once (coords, edges, edge_prob, hyp_cost). Re-solve the ILP for beta in {0.5, 1, 2} on CPU inside the kernel and run the tail once per beta. (ii) Anchor safety: assert anchor counts == 1 for the lowdet, head and ILP-timeout anchors after all patches, and assert the lowdet npz still holds low_coords. HYP=0 must be byte-identical to exp56 (sha check). Check `'node_weight' in inspect.signature(td.solvers.ILPSolver)` in-kernel and skip with a log line otherwise. (iii) Runtime guard: cap hypotheses per frame at 10% of standard nodes (highest score first) and use HYP_MIN_SCORE 0.7 unless the lab picks 0.5. Add a global hypothesis budget: turn the arm off for the remaining videos once wall time since KERNEL_START_TS exceeds (REPAIR_DEADLINE_S - 1.5 h), so it can never push the tail past the guard. Read #34's scoring duration and exp56's per-video 'ILP Xs | candidate nodes' log lines (Kaggle Logs tab, browser_todo) BEFORE submitting. (iv) One lab gate: pooled delta >= +0.002 on 18 6bba SELECTION, and both CONFIRMATION halves >= 0 with no guard trip and runtime <= +15%. If it fails, spend no slot. This raises P(scored | gate pass) to ~0.85, but the unconditional P stays ~0.15-0.2, so the line cannot meet the 70% bar. Treat it as optional research, not part of the 0.99 plan.
realistic_public_gain: +0.000..+0.002 (GUESS; central ~+0.0005). The motion relink rebuilds edges after the ILP, so only the node set transfers. Hypothesis nodes are admitted through edge_prob from an in-sample network, a rule class that has given ~0 on the LB (#29/#30), and they overlap with what readmit/gapfill already recover on x138.
realistic_private_gain: +0.000..+0.003 (GUESS). It could matter more on denser or under-segmented private embryos. Runtime risk on longer private test sets is the main downside: a REPAIR_DEADLINE_S trip degrades every later video.
